text:
Nashville came to San Jose with seven straight wins and left having lost a game it mostly controlled. The Predators had 70 shot attempts to 53, 3.5 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 2.54, and in our replays of every shot they win this one 68% of the time. None of that matters much when three kids keep turning short shifts into goals.

Will Smith, Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg, the Sharks' draft picks from 2023, 2024 and this past summer, did the damage. Smith opened it at 12:25 of the first from Stenberg and Celebrini. Collin Graf made it 2-0 three and a half minutes later on a 4% chance, the least likely goal of the night. Early in the second, Smith found Stenberg for 3-0, a pass NBC Sports Bay Area called world-class, and by then San Jose's win chance was 93%. Graf summed up the line's passing to Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest: "Just a bunch of guys going that was nasty." Smith and Celebrini each finished with a goal and two assists, and the three of them were on the ice for far more than they gave up.

Nashville pushed back hard. Nils Hoglander tipped one in late in the second, and the Predators owned the third, 1.65 expected goals to 0.42 by our count. But Celebrini restored the three-goal lead at 7:40 off Smith and Jacob Trouba, and Steven Stamkos's power-play goal with under four minutes left only made the final 4-2. Shane Wright had the best chance that didn't go in, a 32% look in the second that missed the net, and Filip Forsberg put seven shots on Alex Nedeljkovic without beating him.

Nedeljkovic was the quiet difference: 32 saves on 34 shots, 1.5 goals better than expected, and the biggest single contributor to San Jose's win by our numbers. At the other end Juuse Saros let in 1.6 more than his 24 shots deserved. The streak was always going to end somewhere. Nashville can live with how it played; San Jose gets another night of proof that its young core can beat a hot team.
headline: Sharks' kid line ends Nashville's seven-game run
